guideTitle: Best Air Fryer Toaster Ovens Under $150 (2026)
metaTitle: Best Air Fryer Toaster Ovens Under $150 (2026)
metaDescription: Five 6 slice and larger air fryer toaster ovens at or under $150, including Cuisinart TOA-55, Toshiba ChefFry and Hamilton Beach, compared on size and heat.
expertTake: The Cuisinart TOA-55 is the pick at this cap because 1800W, a 0.6 cubic foot cavity and seven functions put a real convection oven on the counter. The Proctor Silex 6 slice is the value choice for a wide 150 to 450 degree range at the lowest price tier. Anyone who bakes full sheet pans should skip toaster ovens and use a wall oven.
introParagraphs: Moving from a compact combo to a mid-size toaster oven changes what you can cook. A cavity that fits a 12 inch pizza or a six-slice tray lets you roast a small chicken, bake cookies and air fry a family portion in one appliance.

Prices move, and the $150 cap used here reflects live listing prices when this guide was updated. At this cap the ovens add stronger heating, more functions and larger interiors, so the guide looks at which of those upgrades change real cooking and which only change the spec sheet.

products.name: Cuisinart TOA-55 7-in-1 Air Fryer Toaster Oven, 1800W, 0.6 Cubic Feet

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Seven, including air fry and convection

specList.label: Capacity use
specList.value: Up to 3 lb of wings, 6 toast slices

products.description:
The TOA-55 is a stainless steel oven rated at 1800W with a 0.6 cubic foot interior and seven functions, including air fry and convection. The maker says it fits up to three pounds of wings or fries and six slices of toast. That interior is large enough for a 12 inch pizza, a small roast or two trays of cookies in sequence.

Power is the main difference from the cheaper ovens in this guide. At 1800W it preheats quickly and recovers heat after you open the door, which matters for evenly browned food. Set beside the Proctor Silex 6 slice, it adds stainless build and a stated capacity in cubic feet, while the Proctor offers a wider temperature range. Measured against the Toshiba ChefFry, it is smaller but more heavily rated on power.

Preheat for five minutes before air frying, and use the supplied basket on the middle rack. Wipe the stainless with a damp cloth when cool, and empty the crumb tray weekly. At 1800W it draws about fifteen amps, so run it alone on its circuit. For crisp results in the basket, pat wet foods dry, toss them lightly in oil and leave space between pieces so air reaches every surface.
products.bestFor: Families who want strong heat and a roomy stainless cavity.

products.name: Proctor Silex 6 Slice Air Fryer Toaster Oven, 150 to 450 Degree Range
products.description:
The Proctor Silex 6 slice offers air fry, bake, broil and toast functions with an adjustable temperature from 150 to 450 degrees Fahrenheit. The low end of that range is useful for warming food and dehydrating, which most small ovens do not reach. Its Simply-Crisp convection function circulates air around food so the surface browns with little oil.

It is the least expensive six-slice option here, and the simplicity shows in the four-function layout. Against the Hamilton Beach 6 slice, it has a documented temperature range, while the Hamilton Beach adds pizza and reheat presets. Next to the Cuisinart TOA-55, it gives up power and stainless construction but costs much less on the price tier.

Use the lowest setting for keeping dinner warm for guests, and the highest for crisping. Wipe the walls after each greasy cook, and empty the crumb tray weekly. A six-slice cavity holds a 12 inch pizza, but check the rack position so the cheese does not touch the top element. The low end of the range is the sleeper feature: a 170 degree setting holds a roast warm without drying it, and a 150 degree setting can dehydrate herbs or fruit slices if the maker allows long run times. Check the timer maximum before planning an all-day dehydrating job.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a wide temperature range and the lowest price for a six-slice oven.
pros: 150 to 450F range covers warming to crisping
Lowest tier in the six-slice group
cons: Less robust body than the Cuisinart

products.name: Hamilton Beach 6 Slice Air Fryer Toaster Oven with Pizza and Reheat

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Air fry, bake, broil, toast, pizza, reheat

products.description:
The Hamilton Beach 6 slice adds pizza and reheat functions to the usual air fry, bake, broil and toast. A Sure-Crisp air fry mode circulates heated air around all sides of the food, and the maker pitches the oven as a replacement for a standalone air fryer. The reheat setting is the feature that earns its place, because it warms leftovers without drying them out.

Measured against the Proctor Silex, it offers more presets but no stated temperature range, and its cooking logic is aimed at convenience. Set beside the 4 slice model in the cheaper guide, it holds more and has a bigger pizza capacity. For a household that reheats pizza and leftovers daily, those two presets matter more than extra watts.

Slide the rack to the position the manual shows for pizza, and rotate the pizza halfway for even browning. Dump the crumb tray often, because pizza cheese drips. Wipe the interior after greasy cooks. A pizza stone or a baking steel is not a good idea in a small oven because it blocks airflow and slows preheating, so keep to the supplied tray or a thin perforated pizza pan. If a frozen pizza box offers a conventional-oven time, shorten it by a minute or two and check the crust, since a convection fan browns the bottom faster.
products.bestFor: Households that reheat pizza and leftovers often.

products.name: TOSHIBA ChefFry 26.4 Quart Air Fryer Toaster Oven, Stainless Steel
products.description:
The ChefFry is the biggest oven in this guide, a 26.4 quart stainless steel unit with twelve functions that include air fry, toast, bake, broil, pizza, cookies, roast, reheat, bagels and warm. ChefFry technology circulates air up to 450 degrees Fahrenheit for crisp results. The breadth of presets covers most countertop tasks.

A 26.4 quart cavity fits a 12 inch pizza and a whole small chicken, which the compact ovens cannot manage. Measured against the Cuisinart TOA-55, it has a larger interior and more presets but a bulkier footprint. Against the Cuisinart French Door model, it has a standard drop-down door but a bigger capacity.

Give it generous clearance, because a unit this size has a hot exterior and a large footprint. Preheat, then place food on the middle rack. Clean the crumb tray and walls regularly. With twelve presets, the easiest way to avoid confusion is to learn three of them well, usually air fry, bake and broil, and treat the rest as shortcuts you can ignore. Measure the shelf above and the clearance behind the unit before it arrives, because a 26.4 quart oven needs room to vent, and a cabinet directly overhead will take a heat beating over time.
products.bestFor: Larger households that want the biggest cavity and the most presets.
pros: 26.4 quart cavity fits a whole chicken
cons: More presets than most will use

products.name: Cuisinart Artisan French-Door Air Fryer Toaster Oven with HeatSeal, 7 Functions
products.description:
This Cuisinart uses a French-door design that opens two doors outward instead of dropping one down. HeatSeal technology locks heat in where the doors meet for more efficient cooking, and seven functions cover air fry, bake, broil and toast. French doors take less counter depth in front of the oven.

The door design is the practical feature: a drop-down door sits in front of the oven and blocks the counter, while French doors swing away. Next to the TOA-55, it has a similar function count but a different door, and a seal that aims to reduce heat loss. Set beside the Toshiba, it is a more compact option.

Check that the doors close fully and the seal is clean, since crumbs on the seal let heat escape. Wipe the doors and interior after use. Keep the rack position per the manual, and give the oven space to open. Because there are two doors, check at purchase that they latch evenly, since a door that sits slightly proud wastes the benefit of the seal. A quick wipe of the seal line after each cook costs ten seconds and keeps the oven efficient for years.
products.bestFor: Small kitchens where a drop-down door blocks the counter.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cubic feet and quarts are marketing sizes, and what matters is whether your pans fit. The Cuisinart TOA-55 lists 0.6 cubic feet and three pounds of wings, while the Toshiba ChefFry lists 26.4 quarts. A 12 inch pizza needs about 12.5 inches of width, and a 9 by 13 inch pan needs 14 inches. Measure your favorite pan and compare it to the interior listed. Remember that the heating elements sit about an inch above the rack, so a tall casserole or a roast on a rack can touch them, and food touching an element burns instantly. If you bake bread or large casseroles often, check the interior height as carefully as the width.

The Cuisinart TOA-55 is rated 1800W, which gives it faster preheating and quicker recovery after you open the door. Low-powered ovens take longer to brown and cook unevenly. High wattage also draws about fifteen amps, so run the oven on its own circuit. Pay attention to wattage when two ovens have similar capacity. A weak oven compensates with longer cook times, which dries food, while a strong one finishes fast and keeps juices in. If you often cook frozen foods, extra power is the more valuable upgrade than extra presets.

The Proctor Silex lists 150 to 450 degrees Fahrenheit, which includes a warming range and a dehydrating range. The Toshiba lists up to 450 degrees for air frying. Dials on toaster ovens can be 25 to 50 degrees off, so a hanging oven thermometer is a cheap check. Recipes calling for 425 degrees need an oven that really reaches it. Many frozen foods print their instructions at 400 or 425, and an oven that stalls at 380 produces pale, soft results. Preheat with the thermometer in place once, note the real temperature and adjust your dial for the long term.

A drop-down door needs 10 to 14 inches of clearance in front, while the Cuisinart French-door design opens sideways. A pull-down door can also hold the tray when open, which some cooks like. Check the cabinet clearance above, since the top of the oven gets hot. The door style changes how the oven feels every day. If you open the oven fifteen times a week, a door that swings clear of the food saves a surprising number of burned forearms. Check also whether the open door can hold the weight of a loaded tray, since some drop-down doors flex when you set a heavy pan on them.

Pizza, reheat and bagel presets save thinking, and a reheat setting keeps leftovers from drying out. The Hamilton Beach 6 slice lists pizza and reheat, and the Toshiba lists twelve functions. Presets are only useful if the logic is good, and you can always use manual temperature instead. Do not pay extra for presets you will not use.

Grease and cheese drip onto the heating elements and the tray, and they smoke at the next cook. Stainless exteriors wipe clean but show fingerprints. Empty the crumb tray weekly and wipe the interior after greasy meals. A removable rack and a flat floor make deep cleaning easier. Soak racks in hot soapy water and use a nylon brush on baked-on spots, while keeping all water away from the elements. Never spray cleaner directly into the oven, because the liquid can seep behind the control panel and into the wiring.

specDecoder.meaning: The total electrical power of the heating elements. Higher power preheats faster and recovers faster.
specDecoder.watchFor: The TOA-55 is rated 1800W, and most others do not state a wattage.

specDecoder.meaning: The interior volume in cubic feet. It is roughly 17 liters, or about 18 quarts.
specDecoder.watchFor: The TOA-55 lists it, while the Toshiba lists 26.4 quarts, so the two are not directly comparable.

specDecoder.meaning: The adjustable temperature range. A low end allows warming and a high end allows crisping.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Proctor Silex lists the full range, so check others against your recipes.

specDecoder.meaning: A door seal that keeps heat in where the doors meet. It reduces heat loss and improves efficiency.
specDecoder.watchFor: The French-door Cuisinart carries it, so keep the seal clean.

specDecoder.meaning: The number of cooking presets. Many are variants of the same heating mode.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Toshiba lists twelve, but a few core modes do most of the work.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated power and capacity, from the TOA-55's 1800W and 0.6 cubic feet to the Toshiba's 26.4 quarts. Real pan fit counted more than the headline unit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Temperature and presets
howWeEvaluated.description: The Proctor Silex's 150 to 450F range and the Hamilton Beach's pizza and reheat presets were weighed. We favored presets that save steps over presets that repeat a mode.

howWeEvaluated.title: Door and seal design
howWeEvaluated.description: The Cuisinart French-door design and HeatSeal were compared with standard drop-down doors. A design that saves counter depth scored for small kitchens.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and cleaning
howWeEvaluated.description: Stainless bodies on the Cuisinart and Toshiba were compared with plastic and mixed designs. Crumb trays and interior finish informed the cleaning notes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit at the cap
howWeEvaluated.description: Every item is at or under the cap on its live listing. We favored heat and capacity over decorative features.

cards.label: Drop-down door
cards.text: Simple and sturdy, and the open door can act as a shelf, but it blocks the counter in front.

cards.label: French doors (Cuisinart Artisan)
cards.text: They open sideways and save depth, but there are two doors and a seal to keep clean.

howToChoose.note: Pick French doors for tight counters and a drop-down for a simple build.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A cavity that fits a 12 inch pizza or a tray of chicken, strong preheating and a reheat setting. A timer longer than 30 minutes helps roasts.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Cuisinart TOA-55 and Toshiba ChefFry fit this best, and the Hamilton Beach adds reheat for leftovers.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a countertop oven that replaces a wall oven for most meals, with a larger interior, a probe thermometer and precise digital controls.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You use the oven for toast and reheating, in which case a basic six-slice model is enough.

maintenance.why: Burnt crumbs smoke and can ignite. A clean tray also keeps airflow free beneath the bottom element.
Grease bakes on and smokes at the next cook. Use a damp cloth when the oven is cool.
Crumbs on a seal let heat escape. Wipe it with a damp cloth.
Dials drift by 25 to 50F. An oven thermometer shows the real heat.
Grease builds up and affects flavor. Soak and wash by hand.

faq.q: Is a larger toaster oven worth the counter space?
faq.a: It is if you cook for three or more people or roast chicken. For one or two people, a compact combo handles daily cooking.

faq.q: What does the $150 cap buy compared with lower caps?
faq.a: It buys six-slice and larger ovens with more power and presets. The cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated.

faq.q: How long do these ovens last?
faq.a: Four to six years of regular use. Door hinges, timers and heating elements are the wear points.

faq.q: Can I bake cookies in them?
faq.a: Yes. A 12 inch tray fits two dozen cookies in most six-slice ovens, though batches are smaller than in a full oven.
Yes, for five minutes or so. A cold start browns unevenly.

faq.q: Why does the oven trip the breaker?
faq.a: High wattage ovens draw a lot of current. Run the oven alone on its circuit.
